replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always been my favorite subject since school, and I still enjoy solving problems. My master's degree in history involved a lot of quantitative analysis, which helped me appreciate math's practical applications. I find it logical and satisfying to work through complex problems.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I don't get anxious about math because I've used it practically throughout my life. My part-time job involves data analysis, and I've always found math intuitive and straightforward. I prefer to tackle problems step by step without stress.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Last year, I used an AI tool to check my homework solutions. It was helpful for verifying answers but not for teaching concepts. I found it efficient for quick checks but not for deep understanding.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Then, substitute these x-values into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points are where the slope is zero, indicating local maxima or minima.
